evidence.detail: rs/b extends java.awt.Canvas, stores one Component, and forwards update(Graphics) and paint(Graphics) directly to that wrapped Component.
R48 RSApplet (rs/C) constructs rs/b with itself, stores it as the active drawing component and returns it from the applet's component-selection path when the standalone frame is not used.
rs/b owns the client-specific focus suppression/requestFocus behavior and delegates size/location to Canvas while consulting the live Client/Launcher dimensions in resizable mode.

candidates.note: RSCanvas is the conservative legacy-client semantic name for the applet-owned forwarding Canvas wrapper; exact v308 behavior is primary authority.

evidence.detail: rs/i exposes one path-to-byte[] reader, one InputStream-to-byte[] reader, one path+byte[] writer and one file-exists predicate using FileInputStream/FileOutputStream/File.exists.

The class owns three static integer counters initialized to zero; successful file reads increment the first and successful writes increment the second and third, matching the classic FileOperations-style instrumentation.
The write path creates parent directories, writes the complete byte array, and emits the surviving "Write Error:" diagnostic on failure.

candidates.note: FileOperations describes the exact static file read/write/exists helper and its three operation counters; it is a semantic/historical recovery name rather than an independent verbatim-source claim.
